description: Legislation is now progressing through the legislative process. Here are some notable bills: Income Tax Credit HB 1000 is a one-time tax credit for individual taxpayers who filed income tax returns for the 2024 and 2025 taxable years. Qualifying taxpayers will receive $250 for a single taxpayer and $500 for a married couple joint return. Income Tax Rate Reduction HB 1001 will lower the state income tax rate to 4.99% for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026. Math Matters Act HB 1030 is a bill to improve students' math achievement. It will require local school districts to establish advanced math courses at the middle and high school levels, providing our students with more tools upon graduation. Redshirting Bill HB 1048 will allow parents to decide when their child is ready to start school. This will allow parents to delay their children's start in Kindergarten. Distraction Free Education Act #2 HB 1009 would extend last year's cell phone ban in public schools to grades 9 through 12. Last year, legislation was enacted banning cell phone use in grades K through 8. Portable Health Benefit Plans HB 987 would allow independent contractors to contribute to portable health benefit accounts and plans that follow them from job to job. State Employee Health Insurance Plans HB 988 would require the State Employee Health Insurance Plans to cover hormone replacement therapy for biological women experiencing perimenopause and menopause when such therapy is ordered by a physician. Expand Registered Nurse and Physician Assistant Prescriptive Authorizations HB 981 will allow registered nurses and physician assistants to authorize certain prescriptive authorizations from five-day to 30-day supplies; remove certain prohibitions on writing prescriptions for minors; and provide certain prescriptive authorization to order stimulants. The Georgia Promise Scholarship has passed its first year. The Georgia Promise Scholarship has passed its first year. The Promise Scholarship has had a successful launch. 7,744 students have participated in the program so far. From the Georgia Public Policy Foundation, "It's hard to say for sure, but the Promise Scholarship has probably had the most successful launch of any school choice program in Georgia history. The state did not report student numbers for the tax-credit scholarship program until 2011, three years after it was created. But based on the number of donations received in the first year of the tax-credit scholarship (about $25 million), and average award amounts in the early years for which there was reporting (roughly $3,500), it most likely enrolled fewer students than the Promise Scholarship in its first year. Predictions of Doom for Georgia's Promise Scholarship are Already Falling Apart.
